thesis: One request, filmed, and the visitor holds the camera. The clean room stops being a catalogue of effects and becomes one continuous picture: a fictional purchase order (PO-8841 from Halvorsen Marine Supply, $18,420.00, with two delivery terms that contradict each other) arrives as a letter that a line of cyan light reads at the visitor's own scroll pace; its twelve manual steps become twelve beads of ink-mercury that roll together into five agents with their volume conserved; the camera pushes 14x inside one of those agents and finds a drafted floorplan; the Interlude pulls out to the cathedral; the same request is then fired up the four-layer film while a trace waterfall times it and a DevTools box inspects each layer; the Enterprise console halts on a 0.61 confidence and prints a paper routing slip to a named person; and it ends as one of 2,318 points of light crossing a night the paper itself keeps, darkening to ink at 23:00 and returning at dawn. Apple's grammar holds the reel together: five chapter frames of air with one logline each whose letter-tracking settles into place, scrubbed moments kept to about a viewport of travel, numbers that arrive settled, and a mono slate under the chrome that prints a timecode from your scroll depth and the real frame rate of your machine. The darks are the cuts (the hero's hold-to-dive to ink, the stack film, night falling on the sheet, the iris at the end), each flipping the chrome white through one shared cleanDark helper. Nothing bounces, nothing is typed twice, and chrome appears once per object: the hero core and its nucleus emblem share one material, the mercury is a deliberately different metal that reflects the drafting grid, and the alloy mark stays on paper. The three generated chapters (interlude plate, stack film, industry loops and chip rig) are kept exactly where they are and given a story to sit inside. It closes as a film should: a scrubbed build sheet rolls over the arrival plate saying what every figure is made of, and beside the CTA a paper diagnostic ticket lists what this visitor actually did (the request they minted with their own clock, the trace they sent, the slip they approved) with a stub you tear to start. The owner's three asks are the three primary controls of that film, and no mechanic here exists anywhere else on the site.

items.title: The push-in: hold the core, fall through its skin into the nucleus
items.placement: Inside [data-rail="Layer"] (the hero figure); no new section. First thing on the page. Also adds the hero's hold hint and scroll cue.
items.concept: The hero looks as it does today: paper, the decoding headline, the chrome core turning inside its dotted globe, and under the figure one mono line: press and hold the core. The visitor presses and keeps pressing. For the first half second the core does not seem to move, but a hairline ring begins to fill under the fingertip, the headline and labels tremble by a pixel, the film grain thickens, the mercury swells toward the lens and the camera starts in. Then the chrome stops being a mirror: through its skin you begin to see something dark, ruled, lit from within, as if the sphere were a lens onto another room. The globe's dots thin, the swarm parts like a curtain, the core fills the whole frame, and the camera crosses the surface. The room goes to ink, not just the figure: the whole viewport falls dark and the nav and rail flip to white. You are inside a near-black dome ruled with a faint drafting grid, facing the Triseno TS cast in the same liquid chrome you just fell through, the size of the screen, turning slowly, two cyan routes orbiting it. The caption prints 'The layer underneath' and a request ID stamped with your own local time. Let go at any instant and the whole shot runs backwards, faster, until the paper is back and the globe turning, and the mercury wobbles once as the surface closes. A short tap gives a half-second peek, so a click is never nothing. Keyboard holds Space; a phone holds a thumb.
items.mechanics: LIBRARIES: plain three.js inside the existing IntelligenceCore (same WebGLRenderer alpha:true, same PMREM, same chromeMaterial(env) factory, same Raycaster, IO and visibilitychange gating) + gsap for three tweens. STATE: one plain object dive = { v: 0 } plus flags held, armed, pressedAt, crossed; everything below is a pure function of dive.v evaluated in the existing draw() each frame; no React state, no per-frame tweens. INPUT -> SCALAR: press -> gsap.to(dive, { v: 1, duration: 1.0, ease: 'none', overwrite: true }) (eases are baked into the mappings below so the fall accelerates and the arrival decelerates); release -> gsap.to(dive, { v: 0, duration: 0.75, ease: 'power2.out', overwrite: true }); tap (held < 220 ms) -> gsap.to(dive, { v: 0.25, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out', yoyo: true, repeat: 1, overwrite: true }). OUTER SCENE as f(v): u = easeInCubic(saturate(v / 0.7)); camera.position.z = lerp(zHome, 1.15, u) where zHome is re-read every frame from the existing resize rule (w/h < 1 ? 7.2 / (w/h)^0.85 : 7.2); fov stays 30 (widening would delay the frame fill); lookAt(0,0,0). Core: coreU.uPull.value = unit vector toward the camera; coreU.uPullK.value = max(pullK, 1.6 * sin(PI * saturate(v / 0.7))) so the mercury rises toward the lens then relaxes flat before the crossing (keeps the displaced skin inside near 0.1). Globe: dotMat, ringMat and every arc ShaderMaterial get transparent:true and opacity = 1 - smoothstep(0.25, 0.55, v) (add a uFade uniform multiplied into DOT_FRAG/ARC_FRAG alpha; ringMat.opacity = 0.16 * that). Swarm: flee term x (1 + 6v), shell radius 2.2 + 1.4 * smoothstep(0, 0.5, v), material opacity 1 - smoothstep(0.3, 0.6, v). PORTAL IN THE SKIN (before the cut): extend the existing onBeforeCompile of chromeMaterial with uniforms uPortal (sampler2D), uInside (float), uRes (vec2); after '#include <opaque_fragment>' append: vec2 suv = gl_FragCoord.xy / uRes; vec3 inner = texture2D(uPortal, suv + normalize(vNormal).xy * 0.06 * uInside).rgb; gl_FragColor.rgb = mix(gl_FragColor.rgb, inner, uInside * 0.92); (vNormal is already a varying in MeshPhysicalMaterial; the 8% of chrome left in keeps the skin reading as glass). uInside = smoothstep(0.2, 0.62, v). The inner scene is rendered into a WebGLRenderTarget (0.5x canvas res on 'high', 0.35x otherwise, RGBA, LinearFilter, depthBuffer true, no stencil) only while 0.12 < v and not yet cut. THE CUT: per frame compute the core's angular radius a = asin(min(1, R_CORE * 1.12 / cameraDistance)) and the frame's half-diagonal angle h = atan(tan(fov/2) * sqrt(1 + aspect^2)); when a > h (desktop 5:4 at d < 1.88, phone 4:5 at d < 2.28) set crossed = true: from then on render the inner scene directly to the screen with innerCamera and skip the outer scene and the RT; the view is already full-frame through the skin with ~0 offset at the centre, so the cut is invisible; crossed clears when a < h on the way out. INNER SCENE (nucleus.ts, buildNucleus(renderer, pmrem, chromeMaterialFactory, arcVert, arcFrag) -> { scene, camera, group, light, envDark, dispose }, built lazily on first arm, cached, disposed in the existing cleanup): (i) dome: SphereGeometry(6, 48, 32) (32x16 on weak) BackSide ShaderMaterial, colour #0b0e0f, lat/long hairlines every 10 degrees in rgba(230,233,232,0.08) (fwidth AA) fading above the equator, plus a cyan radial glow pow(max(dot(normalize(vPos), vec3(0,0,-1)), 0), 6) * 0.35 behind the emblem; (ii) floor: PlaneGeometry 12x12 at y -1.6, ShaderMaterial drawing 1px lines every 0.25 units in rgba(230,233,232,0.14), alpha falling with distance squared from the origin (the 32px paper grid continuing into the dark); (iii) emblem: MARK_OUTLINE's four loops -> THREE.Shape (the markShapes pattern in portal/emblem.ts, y-up) -> ExtrudeGeometry({ depth: 0.18, bevelEnabled: true, bevelThickness: 0.04, bevelSize: 0.03, bevelSegments: 3, curveSegments: 12 (8 on weak) }), merged with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries, centred, scaled to 3.2 units wide (2.4 when aspect < 1), facing +z at z = -2.4; material = a second chromeMaterial(envDark) instance with a new uLiftK uniform (add 'uniform float uLiftK;' to the factory, default 1.0, multiply lift() by it; 0.25 here so bevels stay crisp); idle rotation.y = 0.25 * sin(t * 0.35) + tilt.x * 0.2, rotation.x = 0.08 * sin(t * 0.27); scale = lerp(0.85, 1, smoothstep(0.62, 1, v)); (iv) envDark: pmrem.fromScene of a tiny scene (black BackSide sphere r 10, one paper-white 4x1.2 plane at y 3 facing down, one cyan 2x0.6 plane at x -3 facing in at intensity 3), built once; (v) two route circles r 2.0 tilted 35 and -20 degrees reusing ARC_VERT/ARC_FRAG with uHead = fract(t * 0.18) and fract(t * 0.18 + 0.5), uTail 0.55; (vi) PointLight(SIGNAL, 0, 6) at the origin, intensity 0 -> 5 over v 0.62-0.8. innerCamera = PerspectiveCamera(42, aspect, 0.05, 40) at z = lerp(2.2, 0.6, easeOutCubic(saturate((v - 0.62) / 0.38))) looking at (0,0,-2.4): at rest the TS spans the frame edge to edge. VIEWPORT DARK: AiPage mounts <span aria-hidden data-world-layer class='ai-dive__dark'> as a direct child of <main> (fixed, inset 0, background var(--ink), z-index 5: above .ai-paper/.ai-grain/.ai-glow at -1, below every section at z-10, never masked by ContentFade); IntelligenceCore writes its opacity = smoothstep(0.5, 0.72, v) through a module-level setter; .ai-hero__copy and the hint get opacity 1 - that; the inner scene's background is the same #0b0e0f so the figure's frame edge vanishes and the emblem reads as the whole screen; cleanDark('dive', v > 0.66). RING: <svg class='ai-dive__ring' width 72 (88 touch)> with <circle r=34 pathLength=1> stroke 1px var(--ink), stroke-dasharray 1, stroke-dashoffset = 1 - saturate(v / 0.62) written per frame; positioned at the press point by translate3d inside .ai-hero__fig (figure centre for keyboard); opacity 0 -> 1 in 160 ms on press; stroke flips to var(--paper) once crossed. TREMBLE + GRAIN: while 0.05 < v < 0.62 write --tremble (0 -> 1.2px over v 0.05-0.3, held) and fresh --tx/--ty in [-1,1] (hash of the frame index) on .ai-hero; CSS .ai-hero__copy, .ai-hero__hint { transform: translate(calc(var(--tx)*var(--tremble)), calc(var(--ty)*var(--tremble))) }; html[data-dive-charge] set at v > 0.05 doubles .ai-grain opacity in ai-ambience.css. CAPTION: at v >= 0.62 .ai-core__cap textContent becomes 'The layer underneath . REQ intake-0842 . 14:02:11 PDT' (from session.mint(), which fires once per session on the first crossing and derives the id from minutes since local midnight, the clock from Intl.DateTimeFormat and the zone from resolvedOptions().timeZone), restored to the live route count on the way out (one write per crossing); session.bump('dives') per completed crossing. WOBBLE: when v returns to 0 after a crossing, add 0.6 to the existing pullK variable and let it decay by exp(-dt * 5) (a material response, not a UI bounce). INPUT: pointerdown on .ai-core__stage -> Raycaster against the core mesh; accept a hit, or an NDC distance from the core's projected centre under 1.25x its projected radius (forgiving touch); setPointerCapture; mouse/pen press immediately; touch arms only after 230 ms with < 8 px movement (the stage keeps touch-action: pan-y so a vertical pan fires pointercancel; touch-action: none is set on the stage only while armed and restored on release); contextmenu prevented while armed. Release on pointerup, pointercancel, lostpointercapture, window blur, visibilitychange hidden, and when the hero IO ratio drops below 0.6 (scrolling away always lets go). Keyboard: the stage gets tabIndex 0, role='button', aria-label 'Hold to look inside the core; release to come back', aria-pressed = crossed; keydown Space/Enter (ignore repeat) presses, keyup releases. REFUSE TO ARM when deviceClass() === 'low': the hold only swells the mercury (uPullK to 1.2) and the ring fills to 0.4; no RT, no inner scene, caption 'core . hold to swell'. HINT + CUE (AiHero.tsx): .ai-hero__hint under the figure (Geist Mono 12px .18em, a 4px cyan square) with __hint-fine 'Press and hold the core' / __hint-touch 'Touch and hold the core'; fades out 600 ms after the first full crossing and stays gone for the session (sessionStorage 'ai:dive-seen'). .ai-hero__cue bottom-left of the hero: mono 'Scroll' + a 1px x 28px ink line whose clip-path inset wipes top-to-bottom on a 2.4 s loop (inside [data-rail=Layer] so PauseOffscreen pauses it); hidden under 560px-tall viewports. PHONES: identical; the 4:5 figure plus the fixed dark layer make the whole screen the nucleus. REDUCED MOTION: press/tap toggles v between 0 and 1 instantly; the dark layer transitions by CSS opacity 400 ms; one RT frame and one inner frame rendered per state (dirty flag); no tremble; ring drawn full. NO WEBGL: unchanged empty figure, hint hidden via data-fallback. PERFORMANCE: the RT exists only while 0.12 < v < cut (one extra scene render per held frame at half res); after the cut only the inner scene renders (cheaper than the outer); nucleus ~2k triangles + dome + 2 lines + 1 plane built once; at rest nothing new runs; dispose adds the inner scene traversal, envDark.dispose() and rt.dispose() to the existing cleanup.
items.copy: Eyebrow (unchanged): 01 / Layer. Hint: 'Press and hold the core' (pointer) / 'Touch and hold the core' (touch). Caption inside: 'The layer underneath . REQ intake-0842 . 14:02:11 PDT'. Low-device caption: 'core . hold to swell'. Scroll cue: 'Scroll'. aria-label: 'Hold to look inside the core; release to come back.' sr-only line under the figure: 'Inside the core: the Triseno mark cast in the same liquid chrome, two routes orbiting it, the drafting grid continuing into the dark.'
items.why: Press-and-hold exists nowhere on the site (the contact seal is a drag-then-hold onto a target); a camera move the visitor drives with pressure, reversible at any instant, continuous through the skin thanks to the portal render target, is the hero interaction Apple pages never dare. It fixes the hero on touch (today a phone sees a self-turning globe with nothing to press), it is the page's first dark cut, it mints the request the rest of the film follows with the visitor's own clock (the first real input the page reads back), and it lands the TS emblem once, in the hero's own chrome.
items.risk: Medium. The portal RT plus the outer scene is the heaviest held frame on the page: keep the RT at 0.35x on anything but 'high', refuse to arm on 'low', force highp in the custom shader chunks and test on Mali/Adreno. The cut criterion depends on the displaced silhouette (R_CORE x 1.12 allows for the mercury lift); if the swell is tuned larger, raise the factor or the edge of the core shows for a frame. Touch arming at 230 ms must be tested against Lenis so a slow scroll start never becomes a press.

items.title: First, it reads: the letter and the record
items.placement: After [data-rail="Capabilities"] and the Intake chapter frame, before Compression. data-rail="Intake", data-ch="03".
items.concept: After Capabilities names what we build, the film cuts to the first thing any operations system ever sees: an email. A procurement letter from a fictional Halvorsen Marine Supply sits on the paper set in Geist at reading size, as if printed. A single 1px line of cyan light descends the letter as you scroll, at exactly your pace. Where it passes a fact, the fact underlines itself and a small mono tag lifts out of the sentence, travels across the gutter and lands in a record on the right, where the value prints: VENDOR, PO, AMOUNT, SITE, DUE. Two sentences in the letter disagree ('our standard terms are net 30' and 'no later than 14 May'); when the reader reaches the second, the TERMS row gets a hollow cyan ring and a note, 'conflict . routed to Verify', the first mention of the agent the visitor will walk into two chapters later and of the 0.80 threshold the console will halt on. Scroll back and the letter un-reads itself. Hover a record row and its source lights in the letter. Nothing moves except light and type, which is why it looks expensive.
items.mechanics:
DOM + one GSAP ScrollTrigger; no canvas. Section: data-rail='Intake' data-ch='03' data-fig='intake', class 'ai-section ai-read relative z-10', standard skeleton (ai-wrap, ai-head with .ai-label 03 / Intake, h2, aside). Grid at >= 1024px: letter 7fr / record 5fr with the record wrapped in .ai-frame crop marks; stacked below 1024. LETTER:
with four mono header lines (From / To / Subject / Received 09:14) and five short paragraphs (~120 words) from content.ts INTAKE. Facts are with native mark styling removed and box-decoration-break: clone. READER: .ai-read__line (1px, letter width, background var(--signal), mix-blend-mode multiply, a 6px cyan square riding its right end); ScrollTrigger({ trigger: letter, start: 'top 72%', end: 'bottom 38%', scrub: 0.6 }) with one progress value p applied as translate3d(0, p * letterHeight px, 0). THRESHOLDS: on mount, ResizeObserver and document.fonts.ready, measure each mark's (offsetTop + offsetHeight/2) / letterHeight into at[i] (one layout read per measure, never per frame); in onUpdate compare p with at[i] and toggle data-read on each mark (forward sets, backward clears). CSS mark::after: 1px var(--signal-ink) underline revealed by clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0) over 260 ms var(--ease-expo). TRAVEL: per entity one paused GSAP timeline built after measuring: a .ai-read__chip (mono 11px uppercase, 1px ink border, paper fill, e.g. 'AMOUNT') positioned absolutely at the mark's right edge in section coordinates -> x/y transform to the matching record cell (rect measured in the same pass) over 0.7 s power3.inOut; then .ai-read__val reveals its pre-rendered text by clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0) in 320 ms and the chip fades (opacity 0, 200 ms). data-read on -> tl.play(); off -> tl.reverse() at timeScale 1.6. Seven chips, transforms only. RECORD:
hairline rows VENDOR / PO / AMOUNT / SITE / DUE / TERMS / CONFIDENCE. The TERMS row holds a 12px filled ink dot; when terms2 reads, the dot becomes a hollow 1px cyan ring (two stacked spans, opacity swap) and .ai-read__note 'conflict . routed to Verify' wipes in; CONFIDENCE prints '0.94' for the five clean fields and '0.61 < 0.80' in var(--signal-ink) on the terms line. LINKING: rows are tabIndex 0 with aria-describedby -> the mark's id; pointerenter/focus on a row sets data-lit on the matching mark (background rgba(0,180,216,.12)); hovering a mark lights the row. Attribute toggles only. FOOT: .ai-figcap 'Fig. 03 One letter, one record. Values fictional.' SESSION: session.figure('intake') on first intersection. PHONES: single column, letter 16px, record below; chips travel downward (same measurement); scrub range 'top 78%' -> 'bottom 30%'. REDUCED MOTION: no ScrollTrigger; every mark data-read, every value visible, chips not rendered, the reader parked at the letter's foot. A11Y: the letter is real text, the record is a real
, the conflict note is DOM text; no aria-live needed because it is scroll-driven. PERFORMANCE: one ScrollTrigger, seven small timelines, measurement only on resize/fonts.ready.
items.copy: Eyebrow: 03 / Intake. Heading: 'First, it reads.' Aside: 'Every system starts with a message someone would have retyped. One letter, read once, kept as a record.' Letter header: 'From  a.ravndal@halvorsen-marine.example / To  orders@northline-fittings.example / Subject  PO-8841 . cold-chain fittings, Dock 4 / Received  09:14'. Letter body (fictional): 'Please find attached purchase order PO-8841 for the fittings quoted in March, total $18,420.00 inclusive of freight. Delivery is to Dock 4, Bergen, marked for the Halvorsen Marine Supply yard office. Our standard terms are net 30 from invoice. The vessel sails on the 16th, so we need the goods on site no later than 14 May. Please confirm by return.' Record labels: VENDOR  Halvorsen Marine Supply / PO  PO-8841 / AMOUNT  $18,420.00 / SITE  Dock 4, Bergen / DUE  14 May / TERMS  Net 30 . 14 May / CONFIDENCE  0.94 . 0.61 < 0.80. Note: 'conflict . routed to Verify'. Figcap: 'Fig. 03  One letter, one record. Values fictional.'
items.why: Visitor-made reading as the mechanic: a scroll-driven reader line that annotates real typography and moves facts across a gutter exists nowhere on the site (the Work page's preview trails the pointer; nothing follows reading). It is the cheapest honest demonstration of 'it reads your inbox', it opens the request the rest of the reel follows, and it plants the Verify agent and the 0.80 threshold that Anatomy, the stack trace and the console slip pay off.
items.risk: Low. Measurement must re-run on fonts.ready and resize or chips mis-land; marks that wrap across lines get the underline per fragment via box-decoration-break: clone, which is acceptable.

items.title: Mercury: twelve beads press into five agents, and you can pull one
items.placement: Replaces the cube field inside [data-rail="Compression"] (data-ch="04"); the section keeps its slot after Intake and the Compression chapter frame.
items.concept: The twelve manual steps now lie on the paper as twelve beads of dark mercury along the same serpentine trail, each with its step name set in mono beside it. They are not chrome from a showroom: they are ink-black metal resting on a light table, and what they reflect is the paper itself, the drafting grid bending across every bead. Scroll in (or press Compress) and the beads begin to roll toward their agents. As two approach, their surfaces reach for each other, a neck forms and snaps, and the larger bead grows by exactly the volume it swallowed, so the five agent spheres that remain are visibly made of what arrived: the orchestrator is four steps, each worker two. A thin cyan meniscus appears at each agent's contact line and its name prints beneath it; the two floors draw, the bus clips down, the extruded headline flattens. Reset runs the film backwards and the necks thin and part, which is the shot people replay. Put a finger on any bead and pull: it stretches, leaves a neck to a ghost where it was, and either springs back or, dropped on a neighbour, merges early. The pointer presses a dimple into the field; a tap sends a ripple through it.
items.mechanics: LIBRARIES: raw WebGL1 fragment shader (MetallicMark's sh()/LINK_STATUS/webglcontextlost/loseContext pattern) on one stage-sized canvas; GSAP timeline + ScrollTrigger as today. SHELL: MercuryCompression.tsx carries over CubeCompression's header (extrusion), aside, readout, Compress/Reset button + aria-live state line, floors, tags, bus, dashed trail, the ResizeObserver -> computeLayout(W) (now imported from compressionLayout.ts, which exports computeLayout, Layout and Pt unchanged), the ScrollTrigger auto-run (top 62%, reverse 1.7x) and the square hairline click ring; the cube DOM, quickTo tilt and elastic wave are removed. The <canvas class='ai-merc__gl'> (position absolute, inset 0, premultiplied alpha, transparent) sits between the trail and the tags; a DOM tag layer sits above it. VIEW: straight top-down orthographic rays along -z from z = +64 in stage px, so plane z = 0 maps 1:1 to the stage and the DOM floors, bus, trail and tags stay registered with no projection to match. DPR: min(devicePixelRatio, 1) * (deviceClass() === 'high' ? 0.75 : 0.55), 0.45 on phones; march steps 40 / 32 / 24; canvas bound to the measured stage box, never the viewport. SDF: 12 step beads + 5 agent bodies + 1 drag ghost + 1 pointer bead = 19 spheres in vec4 uBalls[19] (x, y, r in stage px, w = flags/tint) with uCount, uK, uTime; sphere i rests at z = r; scene distance = polynomial smooth-min over all (h = max(uK - abs(a - b), 0) / uK; smin = min(a, b) - h*h*uK*0.25) with uK in stage px tweened 10 (resting, discrete) -> 46 (merging, gooey) -> 18 (settled); eps 0.5px, early exit when p.z < -maxR; normals by 4-tap tetrahedron. MATERIAL (deliberately not PMREM chrome): base ink mix(#0b0e0f, #1a2124, n.y*0.5+0.5); one paper-white specular pow(max(dot(reflect(-l, n), -rd), 0), 64) * 0.9 with l = normalize(-0.3, 0.7, 0.6); environment via r = reflect(rd, n): paper above the horizon smoothstep(0.35, 0.6, r.z) * 0.55, the sheet's own grid reflected as 1px lines at fract((p.xy + r.xy * 40.0) / 32.0) with fwidth AA at 0.22 strength fading toward the zenith, ink below; fresnel pow(1 - max(dot(n, -rd), 0), 4) mixes 0.35 of the environment at grazing angles, 0.08 face-on; cyan appears only as a meniscus: a 1.5px band where a body meets the plane (abs(hitZ - 0.6px) < w) on agent bodies with w scaled by their arrival weight, plus a 1px cyan equator on settled agents (flag in w). CONTACT: pixels that miss the SDF and hit z = 0 are darkened by sum over bodies of 0.18 * saturate(1 - dist2D/(r*1.15))^2 (a rendered contact, matte, not a UI shadow). Coverage AA by smoothstep over the last 1px of hit distance; background alpha 0 so paper, grid and grain show through. VOLUME: each bead i has arrival weight w_i in [0,1]; r_i = r0 * cbrt(1 - w_i); agent j's radius = cbrt(rA0^3 + sum over its beads of r0^3 * w_i) with membership from COMPRESSION.collapseTo ([0,1,2,0,1,3,2,0,3,4,0,4]: orchestrator absorbs 4, each worker 2); r0 = clamp(layout.s * 0.42, 14, 24) px. TIMELINE (same labels and offsets as the cube version so the extrusion collapse, floors, tags and bus keep their timing): per bead i with stagger st = i * 0.055: 0.28 s lift (r grows 8% as it unsticks) at 0.1 + st; 0.95 s slide along a quadratic path (control point offset 0.18 x distance perpendicular) to nodes[collapseTo[i]] with power3.inOut at 0.28 + st; w_i 0 -> 1 over the last 0.45 s of the slide; uK rises to 46 over 0.3-1.4 s and settles to 18 over 0.5 s at the end; leads become their agent at w > 0.6 (DOM tag crossfade from step name to agent name + 'absorbed n'); floors scaleX, tags, bus clip, --depth and the cyan rule exactly as now. tl.invalidate() before every play/reverse so drags and early merges never bake into recorded start values; onReverseComplete resets all w to 0 and radii to r0. onUpdate sets dirty = true and repositions the tags (translate3d from the same arrays; transform only). Auto-run on scroll-in, reverse at 1.7x on scroll-back; Compress/Reset + aria-live state line unchanged. DRAW GATING: IO + visibilitychange, drawing only while dirty || tl.isActive() || dragging || pointer inside (pointer bead moving) || pulse alive; otherwise the last frame stands; one uniform4fv upload per drawn frame. POINTER (mouse/pen only): ball 18 follows the cursor on the plane (lerp 1 - exp(-dt*9)) with r = 0.28 * r0, smin against the field so the surface dimples toward the finger; ignored on touch. TAP/CLICK: the square hairline ring (page convention) plus a radius pulse on the nearest body r += 0.4 * r0 * sin(PI t) over 600 ms power2.inOut; the compressed field fires one pulse from the orchestrator itself on settle. FREE DRAG: pointerdown within 1.15 r of a bead (or an agent body after compression) picks it (setPointerCapture); a ghost body (index 17, r 0.62 r_picked) stays at the origin; the picked body follows the pointer directly (user-driven, no tween) and uK is raised to 40 while dragging so a neck forms to the ghost; release: if within 1.3 (r_a + r_b) of another body -> early merge (tween w_picked 0 -> 1 over 0.35 s power2.out, receiver radius by volume, tag collapses, state line 'merged early . Vendor lookup -> Extract'), else tween back to the origin over 0.6 s power3.out while the ghost shrinks to 0 (no elastic). Touch arming: a drag starts only after 140 ms of hold or 6 px of mostly horizontal travel (touch-action: none set on the stage only during the drag, pan-y otherwise); otherwise the page scrolls. Keyboard: Compress/Reset is the control; beads are not focusable; the state line describes the field. HINT under the stage with __hint-fine 'Drag a bead onto its neighbour to merge it early' / __hint-touch 'Hold a bead, then drag it onto another'. FALLBACK (no WebGL or LINK_STATUS false -> data-fallback): the same arrays drive 17 DOM .ai-merc__disc circles (translate3d + scale) inside an SVG filter goo (feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 8 -> feColorMatrix alpha 18 -7) in flat ink, so the merge is still honest; drag disabled. REDUCED MOTION: compressed state drawn once; the button switches states with a single redraw; no drag, no pointer bead. PHONES: narrow computeLayout (3 cols), 24 steps, DPR 0.45, no pointer bead, tap = pulse, drag with arming. PERFORMANCE BUDGET: <= 2 ms GPU per drawn frame at 0.75 x 1.0 DPR on an integrated GPU (19 SDF evals x 40 steps over a ~1,000 x 400 px canvas), idle when nothing moves; dispose = kill timeline, ScrollTrigger.kill, deleteProgram/Buffer, loseContext, canvas.remove(). SESSION: session.figure('compression') on first intersection; session.log('compression', '12 steps -> 05 agents . 2 layers') on settle.
items.copy: Eyebrow: 04 / Compression. Heading (kept): 'Not Automation. Compression.' Aside (kept): 'A twelve-step manual process, redesigned as a two-layer agent system.' Readout: '12 steps -> 02 layers'. State lines (aria-live): 'Twelve beads resting on the trail.' -> 'Twelve steps pressed into five agents on two layers.' -> 'merged early . Vendor lookup -> Extract'. Control: Compress / Reset. Agent tags: 'Orchestrator . absorbed 4', 'Extract . absorbed 2', 'Verify . absorbed 2', 'Reconcile . absorbed 2', 'Report . absorbed 2'. Floors: 'Layer 01 / Orchestration', 'Layer 02 / Execution agents'. Hint: 'Drag a bead onto its neighbour to merge it early' / 'Hold a bead, then drag it onto another'. Note (kept): 'An example workflow, drawn to show the method.' Figcap: 'Fig. 04  Volume conserved: each agent is the sum of the steps it absorbed.'
items.why: Metaballs exist nowhere on the site, and this is a third metal that reads as a different thing from the hero's chrome room and the alloy mark: ink mercury whose only reflection is the paper and its grid. Volume conservation makes the merge physical rather than decorative, the reversible necks turn a one-shot animation into something the visitor replays, and free 2D drag with a neck and early merge is an interaction kind the whole site lacks and that works with a thumb.
items.risk: Medium. The shader is the heaviest new GPU work on the page: the DPR caps, step caps and stage-bound canvas are not optional; test the 19-body loop on Adreno 6xx with highp and ?dev=low with WebGL disabled for the goo fallback. Drags that fight the GSAP timeline are prevented by tl.invalidate() on every play and the onReverseComplete reset; test early-merge then Compress then Reset in both orders.

items.title: Inside one agent: the push-in to the floorplan
items.placement: After [data-rail="Compression"], before the Scale chapter frame and the Interlude. data-rail="Anatomy", data-ch="05". Pinned +160% desktop / +110% phone.
items.concept: The film does what an Apple chip chapter does, on paper. The five agents from the previous sheet are redrawn as a hairline plan the size of a hand in the centre of an empty page: five circles on the bus, Verify among them. As you scroll, the camera pushes straight into Verify. At three times the circle fills the frame and its interior resolves into a drafted floorplan: five blocks on a square die (PLANNER, MEMORY, TOOL ROUTER, GUARDRAILS, EVALUATOR) joined by hairline buses and ports. At eight times the block specs print in mono beside them. At twelve times a single cyan trace lights, segment by segment, the path PO-8841 takes across the die, from the intake port through the planner, into memory, out to the tool router, through the permission check in guardrails, to the evaluator, where the threshold 0.80 catches the 0.61 from the letter and routes it out through the human port. The lines stay one pixel wide at every magnification. Then the next chapter pulls all the way out to the cathedral.
items.mechanics: LIBRARIES: inline SVG + GSAP ScrollTrigger (pin, scrub). Section: data-rail='Anatomy' data-ch='05' data-fig='anatomy', a 100svh stage pinned with { pin: true, scrub: 0.6, start: 'top top', end: phone ? '+=110%' : '+=160%', invalidateOnRefresh: true, onRefresh: measure+apply }. SVG: viewBox 0 0 1600 1000 (1000x1250 on phones), a single <g class='ai-anat__zoom'> whose transform attribute is written per frame from one progress object as 'translate(cx cy) scale(s) translate(-vx -vy)' with (vx, vy) the Verify circle's centre and s = 1 + 13 * easeInOutCubic(saturate(p / 0.75)) (SVG transform is compositor-cheap at ~160 nodes). All hairlines use vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke so 1px stays 1px at 14x; text is set in SVG user units sized to read 12px at the zoom where it appears (blocks 12/4 units, appear at p 0.30-0.40; specs 12/10 units, p 0.56-0.64; trace labels 12/13, p >= 0.74), toggled by opacity windows only; text-rendering: geometricPrecision, shape-rendering: crispEdges on hairlines. LEVELS: p 0-0.3 the plan (five circles r 48 on the bus, the four non-Verify circles fade over p 0.18-0.3); p 0.3+ the die group inside Verify (a 2x2 + centre-strip layout on a 400-unit square: PLANNER top-left, MEMORY top-right, TOOL ROUTER bottom-left, GUARDRAILS bottom-right, EVALUATOR centre strip; ring bus around; ports 'in' left edge, 'out' right edge, 'human' bottom edge); specs: PLANNER 'steps <= 6', MEMORY 'window 8,192 tokens', TOOL ROUTER 'tools 4 . erp.read, vendor.lookup, ledger.read, mail.send', GUARDRAILS 'policy 4.2 . 7 actions', EVALUATOR 'threshold 0.80'. TRACE: eleven straight segments pre-authored in anatomyPlan.ts as <line> elements in var(--signal), stroke-width 1.5 (non-scaling); each revealed by clip-path inset() along its own axis (horizontal inset right -> 0, vertical inset bottom -> 0) on the master progress (p 0.74-0.96, 0.02 per segment in path order); no stroke-dasharray (ProcessRail owns the stroke draw). At the evaluator the readout '0.61 < 0.80' prints (opacity) and the last segment leaves through the human port with the label 'to a named person'. HUD: bottom-left mono 'ZOOM 1.0x' -> '14.0x' (textContent, tabular-nums, one write when the rounded value changes) and 'AGENT 02 . VERIFY'; the chapter's .ai-label top-right; corner crop marks from .ai-frame on the stage. COPY: head copy top-left absolutely (desktop) or above the stage (phone); fades (opacity) between p 0.08 and 0.2 so the plan has the frame to itself. REDUCED MOTION: no pin; the stage shows the die at 14x with the full trace lit and the HUD at its final values; a static caption. PHONES: viewBox 1000x1250, die 360 units, specs trimmed to the first clause, pin +110%. A11Y: <svg role='img' aria-label='A drafted plan of one agent: planner, memory, tool router, guardrails and evaluator, and the path one request takes through them to a human reviewer'>; a visually hidden <ol> lists the trace steps. SESSION: session.figure('anatomy'). PERFORMANCE: one transform write and <= 3 opacity writes per frame; no canvas.
items.copy: Eyebrow: 05 / Anatomy. Heading: 'Inside one agent.' Aside: 'Five blocks, one permission check, one threshold. Every request walks this floor.' Block labels: PLANNER . MEMORY . TOOL ROUTER . GUARDRAILS . EVALUATOR. Specs: 'steps <= 6' / 'window 8,192 tokens' / 'tools 4' / 'policy 4.2 . 7 actions' / 'threshold 0.80'. Ports: IN . OUT . HUMAN. Trace readout: '0.61 < 0.80 . to a named person'. HUD: 'ZOOM 14.0x' / 'AGENT 02 . VERIFY'. Figcap: 'Fig. 05  An example agent, drawn to its parts.'
items.why: A continuous 1x to 14x scroll zoom with level-of-detail into a vector drawing is the Apple 'into the silicon' move, and no section on the site zooms into a drawing (the interlude expands a window, the Studio opens an iris, WorldPlate pushes 12%). It gives Compression's agents an interior and makes 'an agent' a thing with parts, which no AI vendor page does on paper.
items.risk: Low-medium. Two pinned chapters sit near each other (Anatomy, then the Scale frame, then the Interlude); the 44svh frame between them is load-bearing so the scroll never feels trapped. Text scaled inside an SVG group can shimmer in Safari at fractional zoom; the geometricPrecision rule and integer-ish zoom steps for the text opacity windows mitigate it.

items.title: The stack bench: inspect a layer, send the request, read the waterfall
items.placement: Inside [data-rail="Stack"] (StackFilm, data-ch="07"), after the Interlude ('Scale') and the Stack chapter frame. The band toggles cleanDark('stack') while it owns the viewport.
items.concept: The stack film stays the image: four floating layers, light rising through them, the HUD brackets, the drifting scan line. What changes is that it now does the thing it depicts. Along the plate's bottom edge a mono control row appears: SEND REQUEST, a trace selector (intake / catalog query / lead qualification), a 1x/0.5x speed toggle and INSPECT. Switch INSPECT on and the pointer becomes DevTools: hovering a layer draws a box registered to that layer's slab in the film, cyan at ten percent, 1px edges, rulers out to the frame's edges that print the layer's contract where DevTools would print pixels: 'in: PO-8841.pdf -> out: 14 fields'. Click and a paper sheet pins open at the right edge of the dark, an inspector with three tabs for that layer: CODE, TRACE, LOGS. Press SEND REQUEST and PO-8841 leaves the bottom of the frame as a 6px cyan packet that climbs the stack's centre line through Data, Models, Agents and Interface, each hotspot flaring as it is entered, a hairline trail drawing behind it. Beside it, in TRACE, a span waterfall builds on the same clock: nested bars, the running span cyan, finished spans grey, millisecond labels printing as each completes, a total settling at 1,310 ms under a cyan flag at 2,000 ms that reads 'Under 2 s', the figure the layer spec already promises. Drag that flag down to 1,200 and the spans past it hatch: 'p95 breached by 110 ms'. Drag across the time axis to zoom a range and a breadcrumb appears. In CODE, three declarations are live: a mechanical rocker on 'fallback: human.review' and hairline checkboxes on 'cache: warm' and 'stream: true'; flip the rocker off and the next run ends differently, the verify span hatching and guardrails printing BLOCKED; untick the cache and the run crosses the two-second flag. In LOGS a filter field narrows the stream as you type. Developers recognise it as DevTools; everyone else watches the system run once.
items.mechanics: LIBRARIES: DOM + GSAP timeline (ScrollTrigger only; no MotionPath), reusing StackFilm's stage, sx() remap, LAYERS y-values, hover/open state, dim/focus states. CHROME: cleanDark.ts (new, shared): const keys = new Set<string>(); export function cleanDark(key: string, on: boolean) { on ? keys.add(key) : keys.delete(key); document.documentElement.toggleAttribute('data-clean-dark', keys.size > 0); } with release on unmount; StackFilm mounts ScrollTrigger({ trigger: section, start: 'top 12%', end: 'bottom 12%', onToggle: t => cleanDark('stack', t.isActive) }); Descent migrates both of its direct toggles to cleanDark('descent', ...) and calls cleanDark('descent', false) in cleanup. CONTROL ROW .ai-sf__ctl (desktop: absolutely at the stage's bottom-left beside the 'Built bottom-up' HUD; phone: a strip under the stage): 'Send request' ghost button (paper-on-dark variant: 1px rgba(232,241,243,.5) border, paper text, fill paper -> ink text on hover), a native <select> styled ink/mono for the preset, a '1x . 0.5x' toggle (aria-pressed), an 'Inspect' toggle (aria-pressed), and a mono status .ai-sf__status 'IDLE . example trace' -> 'RUNNING . 412 ms' -> 'DONE . 1,310 ms' / 'BLOCKED . no fallback' / 'p95 breached by 110 ms'. DATA (stackTrace.ts): three presets, each 11-14 spans { id, name, layer 0..3, start, dur, parent?, async? } in ms (intake preset: edge.receive, interface.parse, agents.plan, agents.extract, models.route, models.call, data.vector_search, data.erp_read, agents.verify, guardrails.check, interface.deliver, total 1,310); per-layer config of 10-14 YAML-shaped lines with tokens coloured at build time by regex spans (keys ink, values ink-2, numbers --signal-ink); three live declarations in all: Agents 'fallback: human.review' (rocker), Models 'cache: warm' (checkbox), Interface 'stream: true' (checkbox); generate(preset, config) -> spans deterministically: fallback off -> agents.verify ends 'failed' (hatched), guardrails.check becomes guardrails.block with a 0 ms bar, interface.deliver is omitted, status BLOCKED; cache off -> models.call dur x 2.4 and every later span shifts (total ~2,180, crossing the flag); stream off -> interface.deliver dur + 260. Per layer 8 log lines derived from the spans (timestamp . source . message), the Agents line for the intake preset reading 'confidence=0.61 threshold=0.80 -> route human.review'. Contract chips per layer: Data 'in: PO-8841.pdf -> out: 14 fields', Models 'in: 14 fields -> out: 3 decisions . tier mid', Agents 'in: 3 decisions -> out: 2 writes . 1 approval', Interface 'in: 1 approval -> out: inbox . CRM'. INSPECT OVERLAY (inside StackFilm, over the stage): LAYER_QUAD[i] = { cx: sx(CX), y: LAYERS[i].y, w: sx(CX + 0.23) - sx(CX - 0.23), h: 0.14 } in stage fractions; when Inspect is on and a hotspot is hovered/focused (existing hover state) .ai-sf__box is positioned by left/top/width/height percentages set once per hover (not animated), cyan fill 10%, 1px rgba(232,241,243,.55) edges, opacity 120 ms; four .ai-sf__ruler 1px lines from the box edges to the stage edges with mono readouts of the box's frame coordinates and the contract chip (glass mono) at the box's top-left; click pins (data-pinned) and opens the inspector on CODE; Escape unpins then closes. Touch: tap 1 = box + chip, tap 2 = inspector. With Inspect off the existing hover preview stays and click opens the inspector on CODE (the old glass panel is retired). PULSE: one master timeline run (duration T = total_ms x 1.5 / 1000; labels L0..L3 at each layer's first span start x 1.5 ms): .ai-sf__packet (6px cyan square, position absolute, transform only) at x = sx(CX) travels from y 0.96 to 0.81 / 0.59 / 0.39 / 0.22 of the stage (translate3d computed from the stage rect) with power2.inOut per hop between labels; .ai-sf__trail (1px cyan column) reveals by clip-path inset(top 100% -> 0) in step (ease none); at each label the hotspot gets data-lit for 0.5 s (its .ai-sf__pulse scales 1.6 and the screen-blend .ai-sf__focus ellipse blooms at 0.5 then fades); at Interface the tag flashes once and the status turns DONE. ResizeObserver rebuilds the packet keyframes preserving progress (store run.progress(), rebuild, restore). Speed toggle sets run.timeScale(1 | 0.5). Replay = run.restart(). WATERFALL (TRACE tab): rows in a CSS grid [name 11ch mono][bars], depth indent 0.75rem per parent level; a time axis 0..max(1,400, total + 100) ticked every 200 ms; each bar a span with transform-origin left and scaleX 0 -> (end-start)/axis scheduled at start x 1.5 ms with duration dur x 1.5 ms inside run (ease none); running bar var(--signal), finished rgba(232,241,243,.55) in the sheet's ink palette (paper sheet: finished bars rgba(11,14,15,.55)); failed bars hatched (repeating-linear-gradient 45deg, 1px ink) + the name struck; async spans end with a 1px T-mark; the ms label (textContent, tabular-nums) set once in that bar's onComplete; the total counter tweens a number object with snap 1 and writes textContent at most once per frame. BUDGET FLAG: .ai-sf__flag (1px cyan vertical line + label 'Under 2 s' at 2,000 ms) is a role='slider' (aria-valuemin 400, aria-valuemax 3000, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext '2,000 ms budget'); pointer capture drag along the axis snapped to 50 ms, ArrowLeft/Right +-50, Home/End; spans whose end exceeds the flag get data-over and an overlay .ai-sf__over hatched beyond the flag (clip-path inset from the flag's x); status prints 'p95 breached by N ms' with N = total - flag, cleared when total <= flag. RANGE ZOOM: pointerdown + drag on the axis header draws a selection (.ai-sf__sel cyan 8% whose clip-path inset follows the pointer); release -> .ai-sf__lanes gets transform translateX(-pan) scaleX(zoom) (ms labels and names live in unscaled sibling layers repositioned by left %); breadcrumb row '0-1,310 ms > 410-760 ms' appears; clicking a crumb pops to it; Escape resets; W/S zoom x1.5 / /1.5 and A/D pan +-10% while the waterfall is focused. Row hover/focus sets data-lit on the film hotspot with the same layer; hotspot hover sets data-lift on its rows (others 0.45). CODE tab: <pre> of lines; the rocker is <button role='switch' aria-checked> with two faces in preserve-3d rotating rotateX 14deg -> -14deg over 110 ms power2.inOut, 1px ink edges, no shadow, label 'live' in the gutter; the two checkboxes are 12px hairline squares (<input type=checkbox> styled) with aria-labels; toggles update config state only and the next SEND regenerates spans and logs; a 'Copy' hairline button writes the text (navigator.clipboard, try/catch) and flashes 'copied' 900 ms. LOGS tab: <ol> of lines each revealed by clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> 0 in 120 ms with 60 ms stagger on tab open; during a run each layer's lines append at its label; no caret, no typing; an <input placeholder='filter logs'> above (ink underline field, cyan caret, 120 ms debounce) dims non-matching lines to 0.2 (no layout change); the '/' chord focuses it. INSPECTOR SHEET .ai-sf__inspector: paper sheet (background var(--paper), ink text, 1px ink hairlines, no shadow) docked right at width min(440px, 38%) on >= 1024px, revealed by clip-path inset(0 0 0 100%) -> inset(0) in 280 ms var(--ease-expo); phones: bottom sheet (max-height 46svh during a run so the upper layers stay visible, 62svh otherwise; same wipe from the bottom; a 'Close' hairline button; swipe down > 80 px closes); inert + aria-hidden when closed; role='region' aria-label 'Layer inspector'; header 'Layer 0n / 04', name, sub, body and the spec <dl> migrated from the old panel; tabs role=tablist CODE / TRACE / LOGS with roving tabIndex and arrow keys, the active tab's 1px cyan underline slides by transform, panels swap by opacity 160 ms. Opening a hotspot opens CODE for that layer; pressing Send opens TRACE regardless; Escape closes and returns focus to the hotspot. KEYBOARD: Send is a button; window 'ai:send' (from the '.' chord) scrolls the band into view and sends; while the inspector is focused R restarts the run, 1/2/3 switch tabs. REDUCED MOTION: Send paints the finished waterfall, trail and labels at once; the packet is not rendered; the inspector cuts in; the rocker snaps. PHONES: 4:5 crop (sx(CX) stays in frame), pulse and trail unchanged, no drag-zoom (tap the axis toggles fit/last range), bars min width 2px, span names truncated to 9 characters with the full name as title, 44px targets. SESSION: session.bump('requests') and session.setTrace({ preset, totalMs, spans, state }) on completion; session.figure('stack'). PERFORMANCE: everything is transform/opacity/clip-path on < 80 nodes; the video, HUD and hotspots are unchanged; no canvas.
items.copy: Eyebrow: 07 / Stack. Heading (kept): 'Four layers. One system.' Lede: 'Every engagement builds the same four layers. Inspect one, or send a request through all four.' Head line (kept): 'Built bottom-up . used top-down'. Controls: 'Send request' . 'TRACE  intake / catalog query / lead qualification' . '1x . 0.5x' . 'Inspect'. Status: 'IDLE . example trace' / 'RUNNING . 412 ms' / 'DONE . 1,310 ms' / 'BLOCKED . no fallback' / 'p95 breached by 110 ms'. Contract chips: 'in: PO-8841.pdf -> out: 14 fields' / 'in: 14 fields -> out: 3 decisions . tier mid' / 'in: 3 decisions -> out: 2 writes . 1 approval' / 'in: 1 approval -> out: inbox . CRM'. Inspector head: 'Layer 03 / 04 . Agents'. Tabs: CODE . TRACE . LOGS. Axis flag: 'Under 2 s'. Live lines: 'fallback: human.review  [live]' / 'cache: warm' / 'stream: true'. Breadcrumb: '0-1,310 ms > 410-760 ms'. Logs sample: '09:14:08.412  agents.verify  confidence=0.61 threshold=0.80 -> route human.review'. Logs placeholder: 'filter logs'. Hint: 'drag the axis to zoom . W A S D'. Foot: 'An example request, timings illustrative. The config is real.'
items.why: No chart, timeline or Gantt exists anywhere on the site and nothing lets a visitor fire a request and watch it propagate; the frame-registered pulse makes the generated film functional instead of decorative, the inspect box with rulers and contract chips is the owner's literal dev-tools overlay ask, and the waterfall is a horizontal timed instrument, distinct from AgentConsole's vertical typed log. The rocker, the checkboxes, the draggable budget flag, the range zoom and the logs filter are what make a developer believe the demo is wired, not painted.
items.risk: Medium. Keeping the packet, the hotspot flares and the waterfall on one GSAP timeline is the whole trick; bars scheduled at start x 1.5 ms must match the hop timing or the two instruments disagree. The paper sheet over the dark film must stay inside the section (not fixed) so ContentFade never masks it. Density on a 390px phone: the bottom sheet, 96px name column and the box-plus-one-chip overlay are the floor.

items.title: Console payoff: the routing slip prints out of the rig, and you approve or correct it
items.placement: Inside [data-rail="Industries"] (AgentConsole, data-ch="08"), after Stack; everything existing stays.
items.concept: The console runs its cycle as before: boot, five steps, ticks and milliseconds. On the Enterprise tab the fourth step is 'fallback . low confidence, human review requested', and now it means it: the spinner keeps turning and the line halts on 'confidence 0.61 < 0.80 . routing to a person'. From a slot along the bottom edge of the glass a paper slip emerges line by line like a receipt: TO J. Okafor, Operations lead; WHY; the item, PO-8841 from the letter; the last four trail entries; and two printed boxes, APPROVE and CORRECT. Tap APPROVE and the slip tears along its perforation, the two halves fall away, the console resumes, prints the approval with its timestamp and closes the cycle. Tap CORRECT and one field on the slip becomes a cursor; type the vendor's name and watch it appear in the resumed log before the cycle closes. Nobody needs the phrase 'fallback logic' explained after watching it once, and it is the human-in-the-loop moment the letter, the floorplan and the stack log all pointed at.
items.mechanics: EDIT AgentConsole.tsx: the run effect (keyed on active and run) currently schedules timers.push(setTimeout(() => setStep(i), 350 + i * STEP_MS)) for i in 0..total. Add a haltAt computed per run: haltAt = active === 2 (Enterprise) && !slipDoneRef.current ? 3 : -1; schedule timers only for i <= haltAt when haltAt >= 0; when step reaches haltAt set slip state 'printing' (the halted <li> keeps its spinner and its message is swapped by clip-path wipe to the halt line); resolve(kind, value) schedules the remaining timers from now (i = haltAt + 1 .. total at (i - haltAt) * STEP_MS), appends an extra <li> before 'report' with the approval/correction line, sets slipDoneRef.current = true for this session (also in sessionStorage 'ai:slip-done' so Replay and tab changes run clean), and calls session.bump('approvals') or session.bump('corrections'). Tab change or Replay while the slip is up: cleanup clears timers and dismisses the slip (clip-path reverse 240 ms). The boot <li> additionally prints 'bench . last trace 1,310 ms' when session.lastTrace exists. SLIP (RoutingSlip.tsx): a <form role='dialog' aria-labelledby> paper element (background var(--paper), ink text, 1px ink hairline, width 320px desktop / 100% phone, no radius) positioned below the console glass inside the rig band's grid (the rig keeps its chip loop); print-in: clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0) -> inset(0) over 1.1 s with timing steps(14) (a printer feeding) while translateY(-14px) -> 0; lines staggered 90 ms by opacity; the bottom 48px action row is separated by a perforation: the body and stub are two clip-path polygons sharing an edge with 3px notches; focus moves to APPROVE when printing completes; inert when not shown. APPROVE (<button>): the slip is cloned into two layers with complementary clip-path polygons along the perforation; top half rotates -3deg and translates down 18px, bottom half +3deg and 26px, both fade over 700 ms var(--ease-expo) then are removed; resolve('approve') prints 'approved by J. Okafor . 00:00:41' then the existing 'cycle closed 5/5 . audit trail written'. CORRECT (<button>): the vendor field becomes a real <input> (ink underline field, cyan caret, maxlength 32, prefilled 'Halvorsen Marine Supply', inputmode text; the operator-key listener ignores it); Enter or the slip's 'Resume' button calls resolve('correct', value): the console prints 'corrected . vendor: {value} . resuming' then closes the cycle; the slip dismisses by clip-path reverse. Escape dismisses and approves. PHONES: slip prints below the console at full width; buttons 48px tall. REDUCED MOTION: slip appears fully printed; the tear is a 1 ms fade. A11Y: the halt line lives in the existing aria-live region; the slip's title is 'Routing slip . cycle 0418'. No new assets; the rig's chip loop is unchanged; no second console (the slip is paper, not a terminal).

Halvorsen Marine Supply . $18,420.00' / 'TRAIL  intake 00:00:02 . extract 00:00:09 . verify 00:00:27 . policy 00:00:41' / buttons 'Approve' . 'Correct' / tear line 'tear here'. items.why: It closes the loop the letter opens: the Why sheet promises 'low confidence routes to a named person, with the full trail attached', and here the system does exactly that in front of the visitor without anyone reading the sentence. A printed slip you tear is a physical, paper-native moment no other console has, the CORRECT path gives the page its second real text input, and it is DOM only on a section that otherwise idles after its first run.
items.risk: Low. The halt must be wired to the setTimeout scheduler (AgentConsole has no GSAP labels) and cleaned up on tab change and Replay; dismiss the slip in the effect cleanup so a mid-slip tab change never strands it. Keep the slip to seven lines so it reads as a receipt, not a form.

items.title: Twelve hours, unattended: the paper keeps the night
items.placement: After [data-rail="Industries"] (the console rig) and the Night chapter frame, before Process. data-rail="Night", data-ch="09". Pinned +220% desktop / +150% phone.
items.concept: A chapter where the page itself keeps time. A hairline 24-hour ring sits in the middle of the sheet with the hour printed beside it: 18:00. As you scroll, the hours pass and a cyan arc fills the ring. The paper warms to dusk, then goes dark, truly to ink, by 23:00; the mono type flips to paper-white and the nav follows. From 22:00 on, every finished task of the example night is born as a single point of light at the frame's edge and drifts in slow loops into place, and by 03:00 the points have formed the silhouette of the compressed system from chapter four: one orchestrator and four agents, drawn in two thousand stars. A table in the margin prints one line per hour, counts only: tasks, approvals, exceptions. At 05:30 the points let go and sink out of the frame, the ink lifts off the paper like a tide, and at 06:00 the ring is full, the sheet is paper again, and one line remains: 12 h . 2,318 tasks . 41 escalations. The visitor controls the whole night with the scroll wheel, forwards or back.
items.mechanics: LIBRARIES: GSAP ScrollTrigger (pin, scrub) + one 2D canvas + DOM/SVG. Section: data-rail='Night' data-ch='09' data-fig='night', a 100svh stage pinned { start: 'top top', end: phone ? '+=150%' : '+=220%', scrub: 0.7, invalidateOnRefresh: true }; one progress p maps to clock time t = 18:00 + 12 h x p. SKY: two full-bleed layers inside the section (not fixed, so ContentFade and the paper sheet are untouched): .ai-night__dusk (background var(--paper-3)) and .ai-night__ink (background var(--ink)); opacities per frame: dusk = bell(p, 0.18, 0.42) peaking 1 then held 0 after; ink = smoothstep(0.30, 0.42, p) x (1 - smoothstep(0.93, 1.0, p)); data-night is set on the section while ink opacity > 0.5 (flips text to #e8f1f3 / hairlines to rgba(232,241,243,.4)) and cleanDark('night', same) returns the chrome to white. RING: SVG circle r = 34vmin (30vmin on phones), 1px hairline in currentColor; the arc is a second circle with pathLength 1, stroke var(--signal), stroke-dashoffset = 1 - p written per frame; 24 hour ticks (1px x 6px), the four quarter hours labelled in mono; a 10px cyan square rides the arc head by transform rotate(p x 180deg) about the centre (18:00 -> 06:00 spans a half turn, so the ring reads as the night half of a day). CLOCK: top-left mono .ai-night__clock 'HH:00' (textContent on the hour change only; a 1px cyan caret square beside it). TABLE: a <dl> in the right margin (below the ring on phones) with one row per hour from nightData.ts (fictional): 18:00 212/4/3; 19:00 198/2/1; 20:00 184/1/4; 21:00 221/0/2; 22:00 236/0/5; 23:00 241/0/3; 00:00 229/0/6; 01:00 207/0/2; 02:00 194/0/4; 03:00 176/0/3; 04:00 161/0/5; 05:00 159/0/3 (tasks sum 2,318; approvals + exceptions sum 41); each row reveals by clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> 0 when t passes the hour (toggle, so scrolling back hides it again; 260 ms); the final line at p >= 0.97: '12 h . 2,318 tasks . 41 escalations . 0 unhandled' plus the foot. CONSTELLATION: a stage-sized 2D canvas (DPR <= 1.5, <= 1.0 on phones) draws N = sum of tasks born so far points (max 2,318) as 1.5px squares (paper colour at 0.85 alpha; every 16th in var(--signal)); each point i has seed s_i, birth time b_i (spread across its hour), an edge entry point, and a target in one of five clusters: the orchestrator (centre, r 9vmin, 40% of points) and four agents at the compass points (r 6vmin, 15% each) with a Gaussian spread; position = mix(entry + loopDrift(s_i, t), target + jitter(s_i), easeOutCubic(saturate((t - b_i) / 2.4 h))) where loopDrift is the sin/cos loop (x = sin(a) R, y = cos(a) r alternating by s_i); from p 0.88 (05:30) the mix reverses toward entry + (0, +0.6 stage) so the stars sink out; alpha fades with the ink layer so nothing bright survives on paper. The canvas redraws only when p changed since the last frame (dirty) and the section is pinned/in view; a full redraw of 2.3k fillRects is < 1 ms. HEAD COPY: top-left on desktop, above the stage on phones; fades (opacity) between p 0.05 and 0.15. SCROLL-BACK: everything is a pure function of p. REDUCED MOTION: no pin; the section renders the 03:00 state (ink, formed constellation, table through 03:00) statically with the summary line; the canvas draws once. PHONES: ring at the top (30vmin), clock beside it, table under the ring (rows condensed to 'HH:00  212 . 4 . 3' with a header row), constellation clusters compressed to a 3-2 arrangement, pin +150%. A11Y: the ring SVG role=img with a label naming the hours; the table is a real <dl>; the canvas is aria-hidden with the summary line as its text equivalent. SESSION: session.figure('night'); at p >= 0.97 session.log('night', 'night . 2,318 tasks . 41 escalations') once. PERFORMANCE: 4 style writes + 1 canvas redraw per changed frame; no WebGL.
items.copy: Eyebrow: 09 / Night. Heading: 'Twelve hours, unattended.' Aside: 'The system keeps the hours you don't. One example night, drawn hour by hour.' Clock: '18:00' ... '06:00'. Table header: 'HOUR . TASKS . APPROVALS . EXCEPTIONS'. Summary: '12 h . 2,318 tasks . 41 escalations . 0 unhandled'. Foot: 'An example night, counts illustrative.' Figcap: 'Fig. 09  Each point is one finished task.'
items.why: Nothing on the site reads the clock back to you or lets the paper's own colour be the subject; a scroll-controlled time-lapse in which the sheet darkens to ink and returns is the most cinematic beat available at the lowest cost (one canvas, four layers). It is the page's only data figure that accumulates, and it closes the request's story at scale without a single counter rolling.
items.risk: Medium. It is the third dark moment on the page (after the hero dive and the stack film); the Night chapter frame before it keeps the console rig's dark and this dark from touching. The ink layer must flip text colour at exactly the right opacity to stay legible through dusk; test the mid-states, not just the ends.

items.title: Projection: the session, the slate, the gate streak, five chapter frames, operator keys and SPEC notes
items.placement: Page-wide. session.ts is read by the hero, compression, stack, console, night and the exit. The slate is a fixed bottom-centre instrument (data-world-layer); the streak lives in the fixed paper; a chapter frame precedes Intake, Compression, Scale, Stack and Night; the key listener and the '?' sheet mount once in AiPage; SPEC notes render inside the figures that have them.
items.concept: This is what makes the page a film instead of a stack of demos. Bottom-centre, under the chrome and clear of both corner buttons, a mono slate runs for the whole visit: a timecode that advances with your scroll as if the page were a seven-minute reel, the chapter you are in, the real frame rate your machine is drawing (measured, not claimed), and two small words, SPEC and ?. Fling the page and the drafting grid on the paper smears vertically like film running through a projector gate too fast; stop and it snaps back crisp in a fifth of a second. Five chapters open on a frame of air, Apple-style: forty-four percent of a viewport of paper carrying only the chapter mark and one logline, and the logline arrives the way a title card does, its letters spread wide and settling into words as a hairline rule draws under it. Press ? and a paper sheet lists the chords that drive the page: g then s jumps to the stack, '.' sends the request, '/' focuses the logs filter, Space on the core dives. Press SPEC (or x) and every figure shows its working: margin notes in cyan hairline boxes with a leader, written by whoever built it and drawn from the same build sheet the credits roll at the end. Underneath all of it a tiny session store remembers what the visitor did, so the ticket at the gate can print it.
items.mechanics:
SESSION (session.ts): module-level state + listener set + useSession(selector) via useSyncExternalStore; shape { req: null | { id, local, tz, mintedAt }, dives, requests, approvals, corrections, figures: string[], lastTrace: null | { preset, totalMs, spans, state }, events: { t, src, line }[] (cap 24) }; actions mint() (id 'intake-' + String(minutesSinceLocalMidnight).padStart(4,'0'), local from Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit' }), tz = resolvedOptions().timeZone's last segment, once per session), bump(key), figure(id) (dedupes), setTrace(t), log(src, line); persisted to sessionStorage 'ai:session' in try/catch and rehydrated on mount; a single IntersectionObserver in Slate counts [data-fig] hosts that intersect once. SLATE (Slate.tsx): fixed

at left: 50%, transform: translateX(-50%), bottom: var(--gutter-y) (the same lane as the corner buttons, centred between them), max-width calc(100% - 2*var(--gutter) - 2*56px) so it never touches the chevron or the contact icon, Geist Mono 12px .14em tabular-nums, colour var(--ink) with html[data-clean-dark] .ai-slate { color: #e8f1f3 } (transition 700 ms, no filter), hidden under html[data-warping] like the chrome. Fields: 'TC 00:02:14:08' (f = scroll / (docHeight - innerHeight) mapped to a 7:00:00 reel at 24 fps; frame = round(f x 7x60x24); hh:mm:ss:ff), 'CH 04 COMPRESSION' (nearest [data-rail] by the same visibility logic Chrome.tsx uses, number from its data-ch), 'FPS 60' (1 / frameInterval() smoothed over 30 ticks, rounded; blank while the tab is hidden), then two
items.copy: Slate: 'TC 00:02:14:08 . CH 04 COMPRESSION . FPS 60 . SPEC . ?'. Loglines: Intake 'A request arrives the way they always do. As a message.'; Compression 'Twelve steps a person carried. Pressed into five that run themselves.'; Scale 'Designed to scale, then photographed at scale.'; Stack 'Four layers, one request, one thousand three hundred and ten milliseconds.'; Night 'Eighteen hundred to oh six hundred. Nobody at the desk.' Keys sheet: 'OPERATOR KEYS / g s . stack / g c . compression / g n . night / g i . industries / g p . process / g w . why / . . send a request through the stack / / . filter the logs / x . spec notes on, off / space (on the core) . dive / esc . close / ? . this sheet'. Footer: 'Keys are ignored while you type.' Example SPEC notes: Fig. 01 'three.js . 200 agents in one InstancedMesh . chrome: vertex-displaced MeshPhysicalMaterial, normals rebuilt . hold: one scalar, portal RT at 0.5x only while held'; Fig. 04 'WebGL1 . 12 sphere SDFs + 5 bodies, smooth-min k 10-46 px . 40 steps . r = cube root of the sum of r cubed . DPR 0.75'; Fig. 07 'DOM + clip-path . 11 spans on one GSAP clock . config -> spans'.
items.why: Scroll-velocity-reactive elements, real inputs shown back as data (timecode, measured fps, the visitor's own clock), tracking-settle type, keyboard chords beyond arrows and an annotations layer exist nowhere on the site; the page's gaps list named all of them. The frames give the reel Apple's air between chapters so every figure starts on an empty sheet, the slate gives the whole visit the identity of a film without a pixel of ornament, and the session store is what lets the ticket at the gate be evidence instead of a CTA cliche.
items.risk: Low. The streak must not fight the pointer grid lens (lens is pointer-fine only, streak is velocity-only, both off under data-clean-dark). The slate's centre lane must be verified against the phone's bottom scrims (ai.css body::after) so the text never prints under them; if it does, raise its bottom to var(--lane-bottom). Keep notes to two per figure or the Apple calm goes.

items.title: The exit: the diagnostic ticket you tear, and the build sheet that rolls
items.placement: Inside the Descent: the ticket inside [data-rail="Gate"] (AiGate, data-ch="12") beside the CTA; the credits roll between AiGate and SignOff.
items.concept: As the iris opens onto the dark arrival plate, the gate asks its question and the triangle morphs to the plus under the pointer, as before. Beside the CTA a paper ticket is lying on the dark: a real-looking spec receipt in Geist Mono listing this session and nobody else's: the request ID and the local time it was minted inside the core, twelve steps to five agents, the trace in milliseconds with its state, the slip you approved or the vendor you corrected, the night's count, how many figures rendered, and 'cookies . 0'. Across its bottom runs a perforation and a stub that says TEAR TO START. Put a finger or pointer on the stub and pull: it hinges away from the ticket, the paper bridges stretch as fibres and snap one by one, and past a certain angle the stub comes free, drops with a little gravity, fades, and the diagnostic warp fires, exactly as the button would. If you operated nothing, the ticket says so plainly and still offers the stub. Then, where a product film would cut to black, the credits roll: a single mono column rising over the dark plate as you scroll, not names but what each figure in the reel is made of, in the voice of a build sheet, ending on END OF SPECIFICATION as the giant hairline TS rises out of the floor.
items.mechanics: TICKET (Ticket.tsx, mounted inside AiGate's layout as .ai-gate__ticket in the figure column beside the triangle morph; desktop grid: copy / figure+ticket; phones: ticket below the CTA): <article aria-labelledby> 300px wide (phones 100%), background var(--paper), 1px hairline, no radius, heading in var(--signal-ink); two parts: body (rows from useSession: REQ, MINTED, STEPS, TRACE, SLIP, NIGHT, FIGURES, COOKIES) and stub (56px tall) separated by a perforation of 11 bridges: body and stub are clip-path polygons whose shared edge has 3px notches; between them 10 absolutely positioned 1px ink fibre divs (height 6px). Rows print in by clip-path wipe staggered 70 ms once the Descent's data-open is set (the same 55% threshold that fades the gate content; observed via a MutationObserver on the Descent root or a prop). DRAG (pointer events with capture on the stub, touch-action none on the stub only): the hinge is the perforation corner nearer the pointer; angle = clamp(signed angle from hinge to pointer, 0, 48deg) applied as transform rotate about that corner (transform-origin at the hinge) with a 0.92 follow factor; each fibre snaps when the gap at its x exceeds 2 d sin(angle/2) + 4px: it scales Y to 0 over 120 ms and is removed; when all fibres are gone or angle > 38deg the stub detaches: a rAF loop integrates y with gravity 2400 px/s^2 and the current angular velocity, opacity fades after 160 ms, removed after 700 ms; the body settles back by 400 ms power3.out (no overshoot). On detach: session.log('gate', 'ticket torn . n figures rendered'), then useWarp().travel('/contact?division=ai') (the identical href the 'Start with a diagnostic' GhostButton carries, so the warp and title card run exactly as for the button). Release before detach: snapped fibres stay snapped, the stub eases back 320 ms. While the angle exceeds 8deg the gate's existing CTA-hover handler runs so the triangle-to-plus morph plays during the tear. Keyboard: the stub is a <button>; Enter/Space tears instantly (fibres stagger 30 ms) then travels. Hover: the stub lifts 2px (transform) and the fibres darken. 'Copy ticket' text link writes a plain-text version with navigator.clipboard (try/catch; label flips to 'Copied' for 1.2 s). Empty session: rows read '-' and a line prints 'Nothing operated yet. The page works as a specification; tear here to start anyway.' Reduced motion: no drag physics; the stub tears by a 1 ms fade on press. CREDITS (Credits.tsx, after AiGate inside the Descent, before SignOff; a plain block child so sticky works): <section class='ai-credits' aria-labelledby='ai-credits-title'> with a 220svh wrapper (140svh phones) whose inner .ai-credits__view is position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh; overflow: clip (CSS sticky, no pin plugin). The <ol class='ai-credits__roll'> is translated by translate3d(0, (startY - p x (rollHeight + 100svh)) px, 0) from one ScrollTrigger { trigger: wrapper, start: 'top top', end: 'bottom bottom', scrub: 0.8 } so the list enters from below the frame and leaves above it across the wrapper's travel; rollHeight measured on resize/fonts.ready. Each <li> is a two-column hairline row (figure number in var(--signal), text rgba(232,241,243,.78), Geist Mono 12px .14em) from content.ts CREDITS (an array of { fig, line, notes: [string, string] } that also feeds SpecNote); the title row 'BUILD SHEET . /ai-infrastructure' and the last row 'END OF SPECIFICATION' in Unbounded 600 uppercase. Rows are static; the whole roll moves as one transform; hovering does nothing on purpose. The counts in CREDITS must be true to the shipped build (counted, not estimated); the comment in content.ts says so and the audit is a launch checklist item. PHONES: same mechanic, 140svh runway, rows wrap to two lines. REDUCED MOTION: the wrapper collapses to auto height, the roll static and fully visible. A11Y: a real ordered list with a heading; the ticket is an article with a button stub; clipboard failure is silent. PERFORMANCE: one transform write per frame while scrolling the wrapper; the ticket's physics run only during a drag.

'TRACE  1,310 ms . 11 spans . done' . 'SLIP  approved . J. Okafor' (or 'corrected . vendor name') . 'NIGHT  2,318 tasks . 41 escalations' . 'FIGURES  9 rendered' . 'COOKIES  0'. The page works as a specification; tear here to start anyway.' Credits title: 'BUILD SHEET . /ai-infrastructure'. MARK_OUTLINE extruded . same chrome . portal RT 0.5x . 2 routes . 1 point light' / 'FIG. 03 . the reading . 7 entities . 1 scroll trigger . 0 canvas' / 'FIG. 04 . ink mercury . raymarched SDF . 19 bodies . 40 steps . volume conserved' / 'FIG. 05 . anatomy . 1 SVG . 14x . 11 trace segments . 1px at every zoom' / 'FIG. 06 . designed to scale . WebGL1 . 1-bit Bayer -> 45deg halftone -> colour' / 'FIG. 07 . four layers . 1 film . 4 hotspots . 11 spans . 1 timeline . 3 live lines' / 'FIG. 08 . industries . 4 plates . 1 radial mask . 1 typed trace . 1 paper slip' / 'FIG. 09 . one night . 2,318 points . 1 canvas . 12 rows' / 'FIG. 10 . process . 1 slider . 4 brackets . 1 stroke' / 'FIG. 11 . why . 4 flip cards . 1 liquid alloy mark' / 'AMBIENCE . 1 paper . 1 grain . 1 lens . 1 slate . 5 frames' / 'ASSETS . 6 plates . 7 loops . 0 added this round' / 'END OF SPECIFICATION'. Gate copy unchanged: 'Ready to Build Something That Compounds?' . 'Start with a diagnostic' . 'Start a Conversation'.
items.why: The exit is the flattest 1.5 viewports on the page and the dark plate is inert; the ticket gives the visitor an object only they could have produced (the thesis of a site that is its own demo, stated as evidence), a tear gesture with snapping fibres exists nowhere on the site and works with a thumb, and the scrubbed credits roll gives the film its ending and tells the people who can read it exactly what they just watched. Credits say what the page is made of; the ticket says what you did.
items.risk: Low. The tear must fire exactly the same navigation as the ghost button (useWarp().travel with the same href) or the gate convention breaks. Sticky inside the Descent must be verified against transformed ancestors (the iris is clip-path only; keep the credits wrapper a plain block child). The counts in CREDITS must be audited against the shipped components before launch or the sheet lies; keep the ticket clear of the SignOff row's rising TS.
